artists.biography:
The Lemonheads are an American alternative rock band first formed in 1986 by Evan Dando, Ben Deily and Jesse Peretz. Dando has remained the band's only constant member.

Since its formation, recording and touring lineups of the band have included co-founders Deily and Peretz, John Strohm (Blake Babies), Doug Trachten, Corey Loog Brennan, Byron Hoagland (Folks On Fire), Ben Daughtrey (Squirrel Bait), Juliana Hatfield (Blake Babies), Nic Dalton (Godstar, Sneeze, The Plunderers), Dave Ryan, Patrick "Murph" Murphy (Dinosaur Jr), Bill Gibson (Eastern Dark), Mark 'Budola' Newman, Kenny Lyon, Vess Ruhtenberg, Devon Ashley, Karl Alvarez and Bill Stevenson (Descendents), P. David Hazel and various others.

After their initial punk-influenced releases and tours as an independent/"college rock" band in the late '80s, the Lemonheads' popularity with a mass audience grew in 1992 with the major label album It's a Shame about Ray, which was produced, engineered, and mixed by The Robb Brothers (Bruce Robb, Dee, and Joe). This was followed by a cover of Simon and Garfunkel's "Mrs. Robinson", which eventually became one of the band's most successful singles. The Lemonheads were active until 1997 before going on hiatus, but reformed with a new lineup in 2005 and released The Lemonheads the following year. The band released its latest album, Varshons, in June 2009.

It's a Shame About Ray, released on June 2, 1992, is the fifth studio album by American alternative rock band The Lemonheads, issued by Fire Records. The album features a blend of melodic alternative rock with a jangly, laid-back style that captures the early '90s slacker ethos while drawing on '60s pop influences. The core lineup during recording included Evan Dando (lead vocals, guitar), Juliana Hatfield (bass, backing vocals), and David Ryan (drums), with production by the Robb Brothers. The album’s sound is characterized by catchy melodies, introspective lyrics, and a balance of melancholy and upbeat tones, exemplified by tracks like the title song "It's a Shame About Ray" and "My Drug Buddy".

Within The Lemonheads' discography, It's a Shame About Ray marked a commercial breakthrough and remains their most acclaimed work. It reached #36 on the US Billboard 200 and #33 on the UK Albums Chart, helping to elevate the band’s profile internationally. The title track became a notable alternative rock hit, peaking at #5 on the US Modern Rock Tracks chart and later earning recognition on Pitchfork’s list of the top tracks of the 1990s. The album’s success was bolstered by its memorable songwriting and the chemistry between Dando and Hatfield, contributing to its enduring status as a defining album of early '90s alternative rock.
